title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
lede: Logician Jan von Plato used Claude to digest 1,009 pages of Kurt Gödel's 1940s workbooks, mostly in obsolete Gabelsberger shorthand, and reports hundreds of theorems nobody knew Gödel had proved.

points: Von Plato's Helsinki team had been working through the 16 notebooks at roughly a page a week since 2017.
Given his transcriptions and his own books on Gödel, Claude produced a 650-page explanation in a couple of days, which he checked page by page.
Claude reconstructed a Gödel proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, one definition short; the repaired version passed the Coq proof assistant.
Of 663 theorems extracted, about 400 checked out in Coq as stated, about 200 needed repair and about 50 were false.
Notre Dame logician Joel David Hamkins cautions that separating Gödel's work from Claude's is a job for historians.

points.text: The six-readers claim draws pushback; one commenter's father wrote Gabelsberger until 2020, and others read it as six who also know the logic.
One argues Gödel was too harsh a critic of his own work to leave finished theorems unnoticed; a reply says intuitions short of proofs are still likely.
Logic-minded readers call it a big deal, given how little Gödel published and von Plato's standing on the manuscripts.
People want the notes published and the method shared, to try the same on Linear A or the Voynich manuscript.
